chapter: Los Angeles 1947-48, Rock Island and bebop in New York
title: The Famous Door, the Royal Roost and Milt Jackson's first vibes
summary: Dizzy's big band moved from the Famous Door to the Roost; Joe Harris and Kenny Clarke on drums; Jackson's toy vibes.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: And it was this big band that was working opposite you when you were with Monk?
And this was the time that "Things to Come" had just come out?

No. They had recorded that when they were at the Famous Door. See, that's when they was in the big band, at the Famous Door. And then they moved from the Famous Door down to the Roost. And boy, the Famous Door, they kept it hopping. They had Kenny Clark in the band for awhile. Then they had Joe Harris in the band for awhile. Joe Harris was a beautiful drummer, very underrated. Quite a few people aren't even aware that there is a Joe Harris. He came out here and stayed a little while, and now he's in Europe. He played with -- what is it -- Clark -- big band for awhile, because Kenny wasn't able to play for awhile. And I understand he had a stroke not too long ago, so that broke up the band. But at any rate, this "Things to Come" was so fast and wild, and if you're familiar with Dizzy's band, he would have the saxophones doing glissandos, and then they started shouting and screaming and tempos flying, you know. Boy. And Milt Jackson had a little Christmas set of vibes, and that was a funny instrument that he had. When he got to New York, he had a foot pedal, but he couldn't sustain, you know. And it was like real inferior metal. Little tiny keys, you know. He had to play with small mallets. Then when he started making some money he bought him a full grown set. Whereas he could play and you know, let a note sustain over until the others, or he could get vibratos out
of it. He couldn't get a vibrato out of his first set. Sounded like he was tap dancing.
Did he record with that first set?
